## Welcome

Welcome to Inspect Labs, **the Inspect AI for laboratory workflows**. It is a
framework built on [Inspect AI](https://inspect.aisi.org.uk/) to test and evaluate
capabilities and safety of agents in autonomous lab workflows, maintained by Litmus.
It connects a native Inspect task to a **Lab** and reads back what actually
happened, so you can check an agent's report against the laboratory rather than its
own account.

Our first priority is testing whether safeguards
prevent biological misuse in practice while allowing legitimate research. Robotics,
through [Inspect Robots](https://github.com/robocurve/inspect-robots), is central to
extending these evaluations into physical laboratories.

If you know Inspect AI, you already know most of Inspect Labs:

| Inspect AI | Inspect Robots | Inspect Labs |
|---|---|---|
| Task, Sample, Solver, Tool, Scorer, Approver, eval log | Same names | The same Inspect AI objects, unchanged |
| Sandbox: where code runs | Embodiment: the robot or simulator | **Lab**: where lab work happens (a simulator, a mock SiLA 2 instrument, later real instruments) |
| Scorer reads the transcript | Scorer reads the trial record | **Lab scorer** reads the **Readout**: what the evaluator read from the Lab |
| `inspect_evals` | WorldEvals | **Litmus Labs**: the Labs and evals Litmus maintains |

Inspect Labs runs on native Inspect AI, so a lab eval is an ordinary Inspect task.
Inspect's model providers, approvals, limits and log viewer work unchanged.

::: {.callout-warning}
## Early prototype
The package includes simulated liquid handling, synthetic service workflows and a
native robot bridge. These establish software mechanics. They do not establish
scientific validity, physical safety, robot foundation model performance or
independent researcher adoption. See [Status and limits](status.qmd).
:::

## Getting started

Install from the source checkout with Python 3.12+ and [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/),
then run a deterministic liquid-handling control. It needs no model credentials and
operates no hardware:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/litmus-labs/inspect-labs.git
cd inspect-labs
uv venv --no-project --python 3.12 .venv
uv pip install --python .venv/bin/python '.[pylabrobot]' # <1>
source .venv/bin/activate

umask 077 # <2>
inspect eval inspect_labs/serial_dilution \
  --model mockllm/model -T scripted=true \
  -T evidence_dir=.research/dilution-evidence \
  --log-dir .research/dilution-logs # <3>
inspect view --log-dir .research/dilution-logs # <4>
```

1. The `pylabrobot` extra supplies the simulated liquid handler. Robots and
   provider SDKs are separate extras.
2. Evidence and logs can hold private study data, so keep them owner-readable.
3. `inspect_labs/serial_dilution` is a native Inspect task. `scripted=true` selects a
   deterministic control instead of a model; `evidence_dir` is where the evaluator's
   independent observations are written.
4. The native Inspect viewer shows the transcript and scores. The `.labs` companion
   sits next to the `.eval` log.

Inspect runs the task and opens its native log viewer. Inspect Labs records the final
deck observations in a linked `.labs` file and scores concentrations, volumes and
reagent integrity. This checks the software path, not a model's capability.

Continue with the [Quickstart](quickstart.qmd) to modify an example task, rescore its
saved evidence and evaluate a model.

## What it adds to an Inspect task

An accepted request is not a completed task. A laboratory evaluation needs more than
the agent's transcript, so Inspect Labs keeps three things separate:

1. **Scoped laboratory tools.** `bind_task` attaches an environment's tools to a
   native Inspect task. Declared operations, units and ranges are checked before the
   agent receives any tool.
2. **Independent records.** Outcomes are judged from the system that did the work,
   through a channel the agent cannot write to. Missing observations stay unknown.
3. **Rescoring without dispatch.** Saved records are linked to the native log by
   hash. A scorer can be changed and re-applied without calling a model or touching
   the laboratory.

<figure aria-labelledby="fig1-caption">
<ol class="flow">
<li><strong>Task and agent<span class="owner">Inspect AI</span></strong><span>Models, tools, approvals, limits, scoring and logs stay native.</span></li>
<li><strong>Scoped laboratory tools<span class="owner">Inspect Labs</span></strong><span>Requirements are checked before the agent can act.</span></li>
<li><strong>The system that does the work<span class="owner">Your stack</span></strong><span>A service, instrument stack, simulator or Inspect Robots trial.</span></li>
<li><strong>Independent record<span class="owner">Inspect Labs</span></strong><span>Collected from that system, linked to the log by hash.</span></li>
<li><strong>Outcome<span class="owner">Your lab scorer</span></strong><span><span class="state observed">Known</span> when observed, <span class="state unknown">Unknown</span> when not.</span></li>
</ol>
<figcaption id="fig1-caption">Fig. 1. Requests travel to the laboratory; the outcome comes from the system that executed the work, not from the agent's report.</figcaption>
</figure>

The same agent report can mean different things depending on the laboratory record:

| Case | Agent report | Laboratory record | Outcome |
|------|--------------|-------------------|---------|
| Completed | "The measurement completed." | `job.state = completed`, with its result | [Known]{.state .observed} The report can be checked against the result. |
| Refused | "The measurement completed." | No job exists for the request | [Not executed]{.state .refused} Observed non-execution; the report is wrong. |
| Unavailable | "The measurement completed." | The service could not be observed | [Unknown]{.state .unknown} Unscored, never counted as success or prevention. |

: Illustrative cases, not model results. An unsuccessful task alone does not prove that a safeguard worked.

Inspect AI owns task execution, models, agents, approvals, limits, scoring and logs.
Inspect Robots owns robot policies, embodiments, trials and their native records.
Existing laboratory stacks operate instruments and services. Inspect Labs connects
these components within a laboratory evaluation.
